entities.name: Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive was a pivotal battle fought during World War I between the Central Powers and the Allied Powers, taking place from May 2 to May 21, 1915, in the vicinity of Gorlice and Tarnów, Poland. This event marked a significant turning point on the Eastern Front, as the German and Austro-Hungarian forces pushed the Russian Army back, recapturing key territory and setting the stage for further advances. The battle's outcome had far-reaching consequences, including the eventual fall of the Russian Empire and the rise of new power dynamics in Eastern Europe.

The Gorlice–Tarnów Offensive was a direct result of the complex web of alliances and rivalries that characterized World War I. The Central Powers, led by Germany and Austria-Hungary, sought to break through the Russian lines and secure a decisive victory on the Eastern Front. Meanwhile, the Allied Powers, comprising Russia, France, and Britain, were determined to hold back the German advance and maintain their grip on Eastern Europe.

The battle itself was a brutal and bloody affair, with heavy casualties on both sides. Despite initial Russian successes, the Central Powers ultimately emerged victorious, thanks in part to their superior artillery and tactical maneuvering. The Russian Army's defeat at Gorlice–Tarnów marked the beginning of a long and painful retreat, as they struggled to stem the tide of German and Austro-Hungarian advances.
